QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_23

question.text: A derivatives contract has a notional value of Rs 8,00,000. The SPAN margin computed for the position is Rs 48,000 and an additional exposure margin of 3.5% of notional value is assumed. What is the total upfront initial margin required?

answer.text: Rs 76,000 (SPAN Rs 48,000 + exposure margin of 3.5% of Rs 8,00,000 = Rs 28,000)
Rs 48,000 — the exposure margin is already included inside the SPAN figure
Rs 64,000 (SPAN Rs 48,000 + exposure margin of 2% of Rs 8,00,000 = Rs 16,000)
Rs 96,000 (SPAN Rs 48,000 + exposure margin of 6% of Rs 8,00,000 = Rs 48,000)

explanation.text: The Logic: Total upfront initial margin in the SPAN framework is the SPAN initial margin plus the separately levied exposure margin (ELM). Using the assumed exposure margin rate of 3.5% on the Rs 8,00,000 notional gives 0.035 × 8,00,000 = Rs 28,000, which is added to the Rs 48,000 SPAN margin for a total of Rs 76,000. The Trap: Exposure margin is layered on top of SPAN, not built into it, so the Rs 48,000-only answer is wrong. The 2% and 6% rates produce different numbers and must not be substituted for the 3.5% rate specified in the stem. The arithmetic relies strictly on the rate given in the question, not on any external rate assumption. Note: A fixed 3.5% stock-derivative ELM rate was not located in the cited Series VIII workbook pages (p.160-p.164, p.172), or in the candidate currency (p.176) and interest-rate (p.253) pages. The stem above therefore presents the 3.5% rate as a given input for a pure arithmetic exercise; the question does not assert this rate as a workbook fact, and the framing of the SPAN-plus-exposure-margin add-up is general Indian-derivative margining knowledge.
